A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete, readable versions of the same OSRM research work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–F support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: Section 5 and Appendix E report original model-merging experiments on eight GLUE tasks, including baseline comparisons, robustness analyses, and experiments with existing LoRA modules.

after.justification: v2 retains the original empirical experiments and reports revised Llama3.2-1B EMR results and task-combination variability in Figure 5.

M1.justification: The subspace optimization, eigenvector-based initialization, subsequent LoRA fine-tuning, and Algorithm 1 are unchanged. The extension for merging existing LoRA modules in Section 5.4 also remains unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same eight GLUE tasks: CoLA, MNLI, MRPC, QNLI, QQP, RTE, SST-2, and STS-B. The task-count range and existing-LoRA merging scenario are retained.

E2.justification: The same model-specific comparator sets involving TA, RegMean, Fisher, TIES, and EMR remain evaluated. Fisher already appears in v1 Table 3; adding its missing heading in Table 13 repairs the summary rather than introducing a new comparator.

E3.justification: Figure 5 revises the stated averaging from 'across eight datasets' to the participating tasks and their combinations. This is a localized change to the reported aggregation protocol; it does not establish retraining. Other splits, metrics, model configurations, and training settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The task-count robustness analysis in Section 5.3 and Figure 5 is expanded to characterize variation across task combinations, providing evidence about sensitivity to task selection. The scaling, sample-size, and learnable-block analyses remain unchanged.

E5.justification: v2 Figure 5 adds shaded standard deviations across all task combinations, whereas v1 shows only performance curves and overall averages. This reports variability across task selections; no new training-seed counts or significance tests are provided.

E6.justification: Table 3 changes Llama3.2-1B EMR averages without/with OSRM from 81.02/82.61 to 78.12/78.85 and revises the task-level entries. Table 13 is realigned and its aggregate averages recomputed. Figure 5 revises the EMR task-count curve under the revised aggregation description. Most results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical objectives, orthogonality constraints, eigenvector solution, Procrustes formulation, and Appendix A proof are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central claims about data–parameter interference, OSRM's integration with merging methods, improved merging performance, and preservation of individual-task performance.

C2.justification: Section 5.3 newly interprets smaller standard deviations as evidence of robustness to task selection. The existing mechanism explanations and limitations in Section 7 and Appendix F remain unchanged.

D1.justification: The optimizer, LoRA configuration, sampling details, hyperparameter grids, hardware disclosure, and code/data/model access links in Section 5.1 and Appendices B–D remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works, reference list, related-work discussion, and positioning against existing LoRA-merging approaches are unchanged.

P1.justification: There are limited edits to the decoder-only results paragraph and task-count discussion, changes from 'Appendix' to 'Section' in several cross-references, and an updated version stamp. The document's section structure and overall narrative are retained.

P2.justification: Figure 5 is redrawn with uncertainty shading and a revised EMR vertical scale. Table 13 gains the missing Fisher heading and a complete set of comparator columns. These changes produce limited local reflow; the other figures and overall layout remain stable.

improvement.justification: v2 resolves Table 13's mislabeled and omitted summary entries, aligning it with Table 3, and removes the outdated 6.12% EMR improvement statement. Figure 5 documents task-combination aggregation and displays its variability. These localized changes improve reporting consistency and the assessment of robustness.
